Counts expected publish days elapsed since each provider's end_date,

colored status indicators. This implements a lighter version of the
status endpoint feature (issue #251), staying neutral without baking in

day boundaries and after backfill advances end_date. A 24h max_age
could leave stale values visible for most of a day. An hour is tight
enough for a status widget and still keeps origin load negligible.

Fix IMF parser to read Continued blocks (#318) (#320)

* Fix IMF parser to read Continued blocks

The IMF TSV response splits months with more than 11 business days
into a main table and a 'Continued' table, each with its own
Currency\t… header. The old parser only read the first header's
dates and zipped Continued data against them, producing duplicate
early-month records with late-month values and dropping days 17+.

Rewrite parse to iterate lines once, resetting dates on every
Currency header encountered. Other behaviour (indirect quotes,
USD skip, rate cleaning) is unchanged.

The boundary-bucket test used Fixtures.latest_date - 20, which only
crosses a month boundary when latest_date falls on the 21st or later
of the month. On April 1-22 of any year the 20-day window stays
inside a single month and the test fails.

Use a 40-day window so the range is guaranteed to span at least one
month boundary regardless of today's date.

* Fix brittle peg anchor test by comparing blended rates

The "anchors cross-base pegged quote through the peg's base" test

blended EUR/USD. Changed to query both AED and USD through the same
blending pipeline and compare AED to USD * peg rate. This is exact

* Extract PegAnchor to consolidate peg logic

Moves peg handling out of RateQuery into a dedicated PegAnchor class

- Effective-base substitution (blend in peg base, then scale result)
- Per-quote peg anchoring (matched-base or cross-base via bridge)
- Synthesizing peg-only currencies providers don't cover
- Injecting base_peg.base row for pegged request bases

RateQuery#emit_blended becomes a thin shell calling PegAnchor.blend
and shaping output (round, filter, attach providers, sort).

When ?providers= filter is present, peg anchoring skips synthesis but
unit conversion still runs to land results in requested base.

* Make PegAnchor a pure post-processor on blended rows

Lift the Blender call out of PegAnchor and into RateQuery, and pass

receives already-blended rows in the chosen blend base and applies peg
substitutions, synthesis, and base scaling on top.

The "always blend, then maybe massage" structure is now literal at the
call site:

  blended = Blender.new(rows, base: providers ? base : effective_base).blend
  blended = PegAnchor.apply(blended, base:, base_peg:) unless providers

Base-peg lookup lives in RateQuery (single source of truth); per-quote
peg lookups remain in PegAnchor (intrinsic to substitution).

Show actual observation dates on /v2/rates (#338) (#339)

* Show actual observation dates on /v2/rates

Broadens #338 from "latest path only" to all read paths. Range queries
no longer carry forward — each pair appears on the days it actually
published, with its own date. Pairs that did not publish during the
range are absent rather than projected.

CarryForward is now used only on the latest/single-date path. The
module becomes a class:

  CarryForward.apply(rows, date: Date.today)

Public attrs (rows, date, lookback) plus private helpers (cutoff,
eligible_rows, key_for) that the apply method composes. The old
range-based enrich method and RANGE_LOOKBACK_DAYS constant are gone;

Send X-Robots-Tag: noindex on API responses (#658)

Search Console shows hundreds of rate URLs on api.frankfurter.dev that
Google crawled and then declined to index. Make that explicit with a
noindex header instead of a robots.txt Disallow.

Google documents robots.txt as a crawl-load control, not an indexing
control: a disallowed URL can still be indexed from inbound links, and
noindex only works when the URL stays crawlable. A blanket Disallow
would also lock out user-driven fetchers that honour robots.txt, such

wants. The header affects search indexing only.
